meta.description: Player-intuitive currency definitions. Tier 1 = universal, Tier 2 = regional, Tier 3 = guild/digital/special, Tier 4 = black-market/occult. Use category for filtering. Base gold equivalent for quick mental math.
meta.notes: Intuitive redesign: less clicking, instant conversion, clear gold equiv, acceptance explained in plain English. Currencies grouped by tier.

currencies.name: Gold Piece
currencies.short: Universal reserve. 1 gold = 10 silver = 100 copper. Bank vault standard.
currencies.description: Universal trade gold. Banks accept it because weight, purity, and greed are internationally understood. Slow to move in bulk but excellent for reserves and settlements between hostile factions.
currencies.player_tip: Always keep some gold. Everything converts to gold.

currencies.name: Silver Piece
currencies.short: Everyday coin. 1 silver = 10 copper. Wages, food, road fees.
currencies.description: Everyday trade silver. Common enough for wages and road expenses but stable enough for bank counters. Farmers trust a coin they can bite.
currencies.player_tip: Street price currency. 1 gold buys 10 things that cost 1 silver.

currencies.name: Copper Bit
currencies.short: Small change. Bread, candles, ferry tips.
currencies.description: Low-value street currency for bread, candles, cart fees. Banks accept copper reluctantly in sacks, then charge handling fees.
currencies.player_tip: 100 copper = 1 gold. Don't carry sacks if you can help it.

currencies.name: Midland Ducat
currencies.short: Regal Empire standard. Stable, taxable, boring. Works everywhere imperial.
currencies.description: The Regal Empire's main bank coin: stable, standardized, taxable. Every coin has weight, date, and paperwork trail.
currencies.player_tip: If you're in Midlands, Ducats are as good as gold. 1 Ducat ≈ 0.9 gold.

currencies.name: Imperial Crown
currencies.short: Heavy state coin. Strong foreign exchange when paperwork clean.
currencies.description: Heavy state coin backed by census, army, tax office. Midlands banks accept Crowns as strong foreign exchange.
currencies.player_tip: Slightly stronger than gold. Good for big settlements.

currencies.name: Oathgold
currencies.short: Dwarven oath-stamped gold. Premium bank reserve. 1 = 4 gold.
currencies.description: Gold stamped with enforceable oath marks. Banks love metal and fear cultural consequences of mishandling it.
currencies.player_tip: Premium. Save for big purchases.

currencies.name: Mora
currencies.short: Teyvat common mint. Deep trade habits. 1 Mora ≈ 1.3 gold.
currencies.description: Teyvat's common mint coin. Popular with banks because deep trade habits and reliable minting.
currencies.player_tip: Foreign but widely trusted. Good backup to Ducats.

currencies.name: Mushroom Coin
currencies.short: Old Regency coin. Still works but politically strained.
currencies.description: Old Mushroom Regency coin still circulates in markets, inns, warehouses. Problem is trust — banks check which faction stamped last transfer.
currencies.player_tip: 2 Mushroom Coins ≈ 1 gold. Spend inside mushroom areas.

currencies.name: Peach Crown
currencies.short: Rebel restoration coin. Strong in Loyalist banks.
currencies.description: Restoration coin issued by Peach Loyalists to pay soldiers, scouts, surgeons. Loyalist banks honor full; Regency banks watch.
currencies.player_tip: Better than Mushroom Coin, but don't flash in Regency.

currencies.name: Toad Bond
currencies.short: Rebuilding bond for food, medicine, shelter after Vigilance crisis.
currencies.description: Serious rebuilding bond issued by Liberated Toad councils after barrel-trafficking crisis. Funds food, medicine, shelter, legal defense.
currencies.player_tip: Moral currency. Good for relief vendors.

currencies.name: Relief Stamp
currencies.short: Ration & shelter voucher. Soup before monetary theory.
currencies.description: Ration and shelter voucher used by displaced Toad communities. Relief banks and quartermasters honor it.
currencies.player_tip: 5 stamps = 1 gold equivalent in food value.

currencies.name: Beanbean Bean
currencies.short: Bean-shaped coin. Annoying to stack, surprisingly reliable.
currencies.description: Bean-shaped regional coin accepted along Mushroom trade roads. Cheerful, annoying to stack, reliable.
currencies.player_tip: Cute but valid.

currencies.name: Wario Coin
currencies.short: Wario face gold coin. Weight verified, sigh at portrait.
currencies.description: Private gold-weight coin stamped with Wario's face. Wario Land banks honor aggressively; others verify weight then sigh.
currencies.player_tip: 1.2 gold value. Wario thinks portrait adds value.

currencies.name: Bowser Bux
currencies.short: Koopa military scrip. Backed by fortresses and ability to make refusal unwise.
currencies.description: Koopa military scrip backed by fortresses, supply depots, and Bowser's ability to make refusal feel unwise.
currencies.player_tip: Spend inside Koopa territory. Outside, 50% penalty.

currencies.name: Banana Medallion
currencies.short: Kong Island token for stored banana value. Doesn't rot.
currencies.description: Durable Kong Island token representing stored banana value. Exists because actual bananas vanish before negotiations end.
currencies.player_tip: Seasonal but valuable. 1 medallion ≈ 2.4 gold.

currencies.name: Syrup Doubloon
currencies.short: Pirate port heavy coin. Bankable in ports, suspect inland.
currencies.description: Heavy coin used in pirate ports, shipyards, taverns. Port banks accept; inland banks discount.
currencies.player_tip: Great in ports, bad in courts.

currencies.name: Arcane Shard
currencies.short: Crystallized magic for enchanting, repairs, labs. Graded.
currencies.description: Crystallized magical energy used in enchanting, spellwork, repairs, labs. Guild banks accept by grade.
currencies.player_tip: 1 shard = 3 gold but only if guild grades it.

currencies.name: Guild Seal
currencies.short: Mages Guild credit for components, archives, tutoring. 5 gold.
currencies.description: Stamped Mages' Guild credit redeemable for components, archive access, repairs, tutoring, containment circles.
currencies.player_tip: Don't spend on bread. Save for spells.

currencies.name: Kivotos Credit
currencies.short: Academy-city credit. Tuition, cafeterias, weapons maintenance.
currencies.description: Stable academy-city credit used for tuition, cafeterias, weapons maintenance, club budgets. Needs digital clearing.
currencies.player_tip: Digital only. Useless in haunted swamp with no signal.

currencies.name: Credstick
currencies.short: Encrypted portable digital value. Great networked, useless swamp.
currencies.description: Encrypted portable digital value. Excellent in networked markets, useless in haunted swamp with no signal.
currencies.player_tip: If you have signal, it's real money.

currencies.name: Spirit Bead
currencies.short: Rakasha bead of shell, bone, amber. Maker mark matters.
currencies.description: Rakasha bead of shell, bone, amber, spirit-touched stone. Banks near Rakasha accept by maker mark; foreign banks undervalue.
currencies.player_tip: Story value > metal value here.

currencies.name: Courier Whistle
currencies.short: Toad courier priority token. Movement has value.
currencies.description: Toad Network token redeemable for courier priority, route notes, civic messages, small delivery favors.
currencies.player_tip: Cheap but gets messages through.

currencies.name: Soul Coin
currencies.short: Lower-plane coin with trapped soul. Worst banks only. +20 gold but moral cost.
currencies.description: Lower-plane coin containing trapped soul. Bankable only in worst banks. Very bankable somewhere, should make everyone feel worse about economics.
currencies.player_tip: Huge value, huge risk. Most legal banks refuse.

currencies.name: Blood Vial
currencies.short: Sealed preserved blood. Vampire markets only.
currencies.description: Sealed vial of preserved blood used in vampire markets and ritual economies. Normal banks refuse.
currencies.player_tip: Not for sane shoppers.

currencies.name: Warpstone Token
currencies.short: Refined chaos token. Illegal, corrupting, valuable.
currencies.description: Refined token of magical chaos. Almost every lawful bank refuses at counter; arcane black banks buy through containment windows.
currencies.player_tip: 10 gold equivalent but possession is crime.

currencies.name: Broker Mark
currencies.short: Underworld mark for info, introductions, silence. Secrets are liquid.
currencies.description: Underworld mark redeemable for information, introductions, silence, discreet delivery. Shadow banks accept because secrets are liquid.
currencies.player_tip: If you need to know something, this pays.

currencies.name: Wario Points
currencies.short: Wario shop closed-loop credit. Traps you in Wario ecosystem.
currencies.description: Quest-board points spendable at Wario's shop economy. Not XP, not normal coin; banks only honor if they have Wario settlement account.
currencies.player_tip: Use at Wario shops. Nowhere else.
